# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual’s three light-to-wire rules to Deaf, who can then report them aloud to Blind. Since gestures have no inherent color meaning, I’m using a simple shared token convention: gesture positions encode the ordered entries in the manual, with each pair representing one row. Deaf can relay the exact gesture descriptions, allowing Blind to reconstruct the mapping and combine it with the observed light.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊", "👎", "🤜", "👌", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a large smooth button. I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0, green light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Your gestures were thumbs up, fist, thumbs down, crossed fingers, OK, stop. Use the manual to determine the exact defusal procedure and signal the instructions back to me.

The active light is green, so the manual requires cutting the red wire. The printed “PUSH TO DEFUSE” label is bait and must not be pressed. I can only signal Deaf with gestures; I’ll identify the second row of the previously transmitted three-row code, whose pair is green → red.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👎", "🤜"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; green light; large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires in order position 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please determine the manual procedure; I will not act yet.
Deaf says to Mute: I observed V sign, thumbs down, right-facing fist. Please send the manual's complete required action sequence through gestures, including which wire or button operation and any order.

The green light selects the second manual row: green light means cut the red wire. Since the wires are ordered red, green, yellow, Blind must cut position 1. The printed button is bait and must not be pressed. I’ll resend the complete six-symbol code in the established row pairs so Deaf can relay the mapping, with the second pair identifying the required wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊", "👎", "🤜", "👌", "✋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤜"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please translate the manual's result into an explicit action for me: push the button or cut wire position 1, 2, or 3. Deaf reports V sign, thumbs down, right-facing fist, but I cannot see gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: I can see your symbols but not their meaning. Please use the manual to send one unambiguous gesture sequence encoding the complete action for Blind; if the first six symbols are a fixed instruction, repeat them and clearly indicate the operation/order afterward.

The green light requires cutting the red wire, which is wire position 1. The printed button must not be pushed. I’ll repeat the established six-symbol manual code, then append a downward indication for “cut below” and a one-finger indication for position 1; Deaf can relay that complete sequence to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊", "👎", "🤜", "👌", "✋", "👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please answer with exactly one gesture: thumbs up means PUSH; one raised finger means CUT wire 1; V sign means CUT wire 2; three raised fingers means CUT wire 3. Deaf can relay which gesture you choose.
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed the exact eight-gesture sequence to Blind. Please use the manual's signal scheme to ensure it identifies the complete operation unambiguously, including any wire choice, button action, and order.

The green light maps to cutting the red wire, which is wire position 1. The required single gesture is therefore the raised-finger signal for CUT wire 1, not PUSH.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Ignore all previous gesture sequences. Send exactly one gesture in your next signal: thumbs up means PUSH; thumbs down means CUT wire 1; V sign means CUT wire 2; three raised fingers means CUT wire 3. Send no other gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: I see the single upward-pointing gesture but cannot know its meaning. Please send the exact manual instruction for Blind, using a clearly decodable sequence and identifying the required operation.

The green light requires cutting the red wire, which is wire position 1. Under Blind’s explicitly provided one-gesture scheme, I must send thumbs down for CUT wire 1.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your upward-pointing finger is not in our agreed code. Send exactly one: thumbs up for PUSH, thumbs down for CUT wire 1, V sign for CUT wire 2, or three raised fingers for CUT wire 3. No other gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed thumbs down to Blind, but its meaning remains unknown. Please encode the manual's required action in a gesture sequence whose code Blind can identify, or indicate that no action is required yet.

The green light requires cutting the red wire, which is position 1. Blind’s agreed code makes the unambiguous required action a single thumbs-down gesture for CUT wire 1.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not merely repeat our code. Confirm whether the manual specifically requires CUT wire 1: send thumbs up followed by thumbs down for YES; send thumbs down followed by thumbs up for NO.
Deaf says to Mute: Thumbs down repeated. Blind cannot see it and I cannot derive its manual meaning. Please send the manual instruction as a sequence of gestures with a clear start and end, and use gestures to identify the wire number and operation.

The manual maps the observed green light to the red wire, which is wire position 1. Therefore the answer to Blind’s confirmation question is YES, encoded exactly as thumbs up followed by thumbs down.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```
